title: The Price of a Dream

full_text:
A miserly merchant brought a poor weaver before the court, shouting: "Last night I dreamed that this pauper broke into my storehouse and stole ten sacks of flour! He must pay me fifty silver coins for the loss!"

The town judge was dumbfounded, but Nasruddin stepped forward: "I shall dispense justice!"

Nasruddin placed a polished silver mirror on the table, took fifty silver coins from his purse, and placed them in front of the glass.

He told the merchant: "Look into the mirror, merchant! Do you see those fifty shiny coins reflected in the glass?"

"Yes, Mulla!" said the merchant eagerly.

"Then take the reflection of the coins," ruled Nasruddin. "For an imaginary theft in a dream, an imaginary payment in a mirror is the exact legal price!"
moral: An imaginary injury deserves nothing more than an imaginary compensation.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Price of a Dream"?
options: Foolishness hides wisdom; laughter teaches truth
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
quiz.hint: Reflect upon the resolution of the story.
